title: The live essay harness did not parse, so its two EssayTV source pins never ran
body:
## Summary
tools/essay-ui-test.cjs held a literal line break inside a regex literal, so the file was not valid JavaScript and nothing in it could run.

## Description
tools/essay-ui-test.cjs:26 matched `/const figs:[^<LF>]*/` with a real newline in the character class (176f04f0), a heredoc artefact. `node --check` failed with "Invalid regular expression: missing /", so the harness and its two source pins (the forensic figures include words and links, desk/src/essay/EssayTV.tsx:492; the plan caption shows a refused read) could never execute. Fixed: the class is `[^\n]`, and tools/essay-piece-test.cjs (in test:rules) compiles the harness through vm.Script over Module.wrap, so an unparsable harness goes red in the gate without running a live model.

## Flow
- node --check tools/essay-ui-test.cjs -> SyntaxError (exit 1)
- fix the class; add the compile case to essay-piece-test
- probe: run the harness with a scratch DESK_DATA_DIR and no server; it passes both pins and stops at the missing pairing.json

## Expected impact
The operator's live Essay run starts again, and a future paste of the same kind is caught by npm test. Nothing behavioural can break: the case only compiles the file.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the live harness parses and its pins run
Before: node --check exit 1; pins reached 0 of 2; essay-piece-test against the HEAD harness 54/1
After: node --check exit 0; pins reached 2 of 2; essay-piece-test 55/0
Method: gate - node --check and the new rules case, red on HEAD then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tools/essay-ui-test.cjs:26 `const f=tv.match(/const figs:[^` + newline + `]*/)?.[0]`
node --check -> SyntaxError: Invalid regular expression: missing /

title: rules/docx.ts loaded node:zlib; the caller now hands it the inflater
body:
## Summary
desk/src/lib/rules/docx.ts imported node:zlib, the one rules-pure break tools/desk-boundaries.cjs carried as OWED for this file.

## Description
The zip and XML reading in docx.ts is a rule (it decides what text a .docx holds and what it refuses); only the DEFLATE primitive is I/O-shaped. Registry software-engineering/module-design, technique io-free-core: the decision stays pure and the edge supplies the primitive. docxText(buf, inflate) now takes zlib inflateRawSync's shape from its one caller, desk/src/app/api/texts/route.ts, and keeps the zip-bomb cap itself (passes maxOutputLength and re-checks the output length). The OWED entry is removed from tools/desk-boundaries.cjs (a stale OWED fails).

## Flow
- remove the OWED entry -> desk-boundaries exit 1 (FAIL rules-pure docx.ts -> node:zlib)
- docx-rules-test new case: a spy inflater is called once with the cap, a stored entry never calls it, no zlib import in the source (red on HEAD)
- inject the inflater; the route passes inflateRawSync; texts-rules-test route case posts a .docx and keeps it (seeded red with a no-op inflater)

## Expected impact
The rules folder is pure again for this file, so the owed list shrinks 3 -> 2 and a docx rules suite needs no Node built-in. Could break: a caller that forgets the inflater gets the "does not open" refusal; the route test pins the one caller.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - rules load no Node built-in
Before: desk-boundaries with the OWED entry gone: exit 1; owed 3; docx-rules-test 6/1 on HEAD
After: desk-boundaries exit 0, 0 problems, owed 2; docx-rules-test 7/0; texts-rules-test 15/0 (seed 14/1)
Method: gate - desk-boundaries red then green, plus both suites
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/rules/docx.ts:15 (before the fix) `import { inflateRawSync } from "node:zlib";`
tools/desk-boundaries.cjs:54 (before the fix) OWED rules-pure desk/src/lib/rules/docx.ts node:zlib

title: lib/twin/state.ts wrote twin.json itself; the session's texts.ts now writes it
body:
## Summary
desk/src/lib/twin/state.ts wrote and renamed twin.json directly, the state-in-session break tools/desk-boundaries.cjs carried as OWED.

## Description
twin.json lives in the learner's text folder, which desk/src/lib/session/texts.ts already owns (pieces, notice.json, deleteAll). state.ts was a second writer into it (mkdirSync, writeFileSync, renameSync). The write and the put-aside rename moved to texts.ts (twinFileOf, writeTwinFile, setAsideTwinFile, the same tmp-then-rename as writePiece); state.ts keeps every decision and only reads. Same path, same atomic write, same .bad-<base36> name. The rejected alternative, a WRITE_ALLOW entry, is a policy-loosen.

## Flow
- remove the OWED entry -> desk-boundaries exit 1 (FAIL state-in-session twin/state.ts writes files)
- move the write and rename into texts.ts; state.ts calls them
- desk-boundaries exit 0; twin, error-doors (put-aside case), texts and essay-piece suites unchanged and green

## Expected impact
One writer for the learner's text folder; the owed list shrinks 2 -> 1 (only engines/meter.ts is left). Could break: nothing observable; error-doors-test still finds exactly one twin.json.bad-*.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - only the session writes files
Before: unlisted writers outside session/ and engines/: 1; desk-boundaries with the OWED entry gone exit 1
After: 0; exit 0, owed 1
Method: gate - desk-boundaries red then green; twin-rules 8/0, error-doors 10/0, texts-rules 15/0, essay-piece 55/0
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/twin/state.ts:7 (before the fix) `import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, renameSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";`
desk/src/lib/twin/state.ts:52,62-65 (before the fix) renameSync / mkdirSync / writeFileSync

title: Leaving one exemplar out exported a sixth piece the learner was never shown
body:
## Summary
GET /api/twin listed the newest five candidates before exclusion, while the card took five after it, so excluding one exported an unreviewed piece verbatim.

## Description
desk/src/app/api/twin/route.ts:37 (before c4792ab1) built the review list from portraitOf(pieces) with no exclusions and only flagged left-out ones; desk/src/lib/twin/card.ts:48 drops the excluded pieces first and then slices five (buildCard -> portraitOf(pieces, excluded)). With six or more pieces in a channel, the review step (Twin Card SPEC 14) was bypassed exactly when the learner used it. Registry software-engineering/invariant-placement, technique paired-sites-localize-the-fault: one rule (what is exported) had two derivations. Fixed: card.ts reviewOf lists exactly the exported exemplars plus every left-out piece; the route serves it in the same shape.

## Flow
- keep seven message pieces as an adult; open /drop: five listed
- untick the newest: GET /api/twin lists the same five, one unticked
- download the card: it carries five exemplars, one of them the sixth newest piece, never listed

## Expected impact
An adult reviewing what their Twin Card exports sees every text it will carry. Could break: the /drop list grows by the left-out pieces (same item shape).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the card exports only reviewed texts
Before: exported exemplars absent from the review list: 1 of 5 (twin-rules-test new case, red on HEAD)
After: 0 of 5; twin-rules-test 9/0
Method: gate - new route-level case red on HEAD then green
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
desk/src/app/api/twin/route.ts:37,41 (before c4792ab1) `const portrait = portraitOf(pieces);` ... `exemplars: c.exemplars.map((e) => ({ ...e, included: !excluded.has(e.pieceId) }))`
desk/src/lib/twin/card.ts:48 `ps.filter((p) => !excluded.has(p.id) && ownText(...)).slice(0, EXEMPLARS_PER_CHANNEL)`
Red: "exported but never shown for review: \"ok see you at the pub — mine is a pint\""

title: The empty Workroom sent the exemplar review to a phone that has none
body:
## Summary
desk/src/essay/Workroom.tsx:54 said the card's texts are reviewed "on your phone" and that only messages or emails count toward birth.

## Description
Only /drop (the PC page) fetches /api/twin and shows the include boxes; no file under desk/src/app/phone reaches /api/twin (grep: 0 hits). channelOf (desk/src/lib/twin/card.ts:25) puts every other format in the generic channel, which the same screen lists as "Essays" and which is born at three too. The line now reads "kept pieces of one kind: messages, emails or essays ... which you review on the PC page", matching the screen's own "Download its card on the PC page".

## Flow
- an adult with nothing kept opens Essay Master: the Workroom's twin panel shows the empty line
- it directs them to the phone, which has no twin view
- server render of WorkroomScreen in twin-rules-test pins the new line and that no phone file reaches /api/twin

## Expected impact
The learner goes to the surface that has the review. Could break: the line is 14 characters longer on the TV (owed capture).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the copy names the surface that has the review
Before: surfaces named that lack the review: 1; kinds named of the 3 that are born: 2; twin-rules-test 9/1
After: 0; 3; 10/0
Method: gate - server render, red on HEAD then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/essay/Workroom.tsx:54 (before the fix) "...the card carries up to five of your own texts, which you review on your phone..."
grep -rn "/api/twin" desk/src/app/phone -> 0 hits; desk/src/app/drop/page.tsx:36,64 fetch("/api/twin")

title: workroomOf re-diffed every piece on every keep and twin call
body:
## Summary
desk/src/lib/twin/workroom.ts re-ran the quadratic sentence LCS for every kept piece each time the Workroom was built.

## Description
workroomOf runs on every keep (/api/texts refresh) and every /api/twin GET and POST. versionDiff (desk/src/lib/rules/diff.ts:145) is O(n*m) in sentences with an array-of-arrays table. At the declared caps (TEXT_PIECES_MAX 50, TEXT_VERSION_MAX_CHARS 100 KB) that held the server's one thread for ~2.8-4 s per call, stalling the SSE stream the TV renders from. Versions only append (addVersion refuses at TEXT_VERSIONS_MAX), so the piece id, version count, last version time and both lengths name a pair; lastDiff memoises it in a bounded (500) derived map.

## Flow
- probe: 50 pieces x 2 versions x 100 KB in a scratch DESK_DATA_DIR
- call workroomOf twice, then once after one new version
- texts-rules-test: an unchanged piece returns the same diff object; a new version is re-diffed

## Expected impact
At the caps a keep no longer freezes the desk for seconds. Could break: a stale diff if a piece file were edited in place outside texts.ts (lengths are in the key).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - steady-state Workroom build at the caps
Before: second call 3848 ms; after one keep 3985 ms
After: 351 ms; 510 ms (cold first call unchanged, ~2.8 s)
Method: gate - texts-rules-test red on HEAD (15/1) then green (16/0), plus the timing probe on both trees
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/twin/workroom.ts:23 (before 097456ee) `diff: v.length >= 2 ? versionDiff(v[v.length - 2].text, v[v.length - 1].text) : null`
probe HEAD: call 1 2820 ms, call 2 3848 ms, after keep 3985 ms; fixed: 2881 / 351 / 510 ms

title: The card's dash allowance and the style meter used two clause-dash rules
body:
## Summary
desk/src/lib/rules/style.ts and desk/src/lib/twin/card.ts each had their own clause-dash regex and disagreed on 3 of 9 forms.

## Description
The sheet counted `/\s[-–—]\s|—/g` (style.ts:104); buildCard decided dash_policy with `/\s[-–—]\s|\w—\w/` (card.ts:92). An em dash glued to one side ("ok— see you", "ok —see you", "well, —fine") was a dash for the meter and "avoid" on the exported card, which tells every tool that loads it to avoid dashes the person writes. style.ts now exports CLAUSE_DASH and both sites use it.

## Flow
- twin-rules-test new case: nine forms, each as an exemplar of a born card
- assert the card's dash_policy matches the sheet's dash rate for the same text
- red on HEAD at "ok— see you"; green after the shared rule

## Expected impact
A card reflects the dashes the person actually writes. Could break: three forms now export "allow" where they exported "avoid".

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one rule for one judgement
Before: forms where the two rules disagree: 3 of 9; twin-rules-test 10/1
After: 0 of 9; 11/0
Method: gate - new case red on HEAD then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/rules/style.ts:104 (before the fix) dash: pm(count(all, /\s[-–—]\s|—/g), S)
desk/src/lib/twin/card.ts:92 (before the fix) /\s[-–—]\s|\w—\w/
probe: "ok— see you" card avoid, sheet dash 1000

title: The Workroom breaks Specimen's type floor at five rules and can overflow the stage
body:
## Summary
desk/src/design/essay-specimen.css sets five Workroom rules below the floor docs/DESIGN-ESSAY-MASTER.md:41 states, and three born channels stack past the bottom safe zone.

## Description
The design doc says "Nothing under 28 px except 20-22 px mono labels, which never carry a meaning alone". The Workroom has .em-wr-list .m 26 px (version and paragraph counts, :269), .em-tag 18 px mono (:270), .em-twin-ch dl div 24 px (the level words, a meaning alone, :283), dt 18 px mono (:284), .em-wr-note 24 px (a sentence, :285). The twin aside starts at top 200 px with no height limit; a born channel holds a header plus eight level-word rows, roughly 356 px at the current sizes, so three born channels reach ~1270 px on a 1080 stage, and raising the rows to 28 px makes it worse. Fixing the floor needs a layout decision (two columns of level words, or only the focused channel expanded), not a size bump.

## Flow
- an adult keeps three messages, three emails and three essays
- the Workroom shows three born channels, each with eight level words
- walk: the aside runs past y 1026 (simulation from the CSS box sizes; no capture possible in this run)
- build: lay the level words out two per row or collapse unfocused channels, then lift the five rules to the floor

## Expected impact
Level words readable from the sofa and nothing clipped off the TV. Could break: the Workroom's composition; needs the capture on both arms.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - legible, in-frame Workroom
Before: 5 rules under the floor; 3 born channels ~1270 px tall from y 200 (computed)
After: 0 rules under the floor; aside bottom <= 1026 px (predicted)
Method: simulation - box sizes walked from the CSS; no dev server in this run for a capture
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/design/essay-specimen.css:269 font-size: 26px; :270 18px; :283 24px; :284 18px; :285 24px; :277 .em-twin top: 200px, no max-height
docs/DESIGN-ESSAY-MASTER.md:41 "Nothing under 28 px except 20-22 px mono labels"
instrument: A Playwright capture of /tv on a seeded DESK_DATA_DIR with three born channels (3 messages, 3 emails, 3 essays) at 1920x1080, measuring the .em-twin bottom against the 5% safe zone (<= 1026 px), on both arms; plus a CSS rows test that every font-size in desk/src/design/essay-specimen.css is >= 28 px or a 20-22 px mono label.

title: The shelf vanishes on a failed load, taking the delete controls with it
body:
## Summary
desk/src/app/phone/EssayShelf.tsx renders nothing while loading and nothing on a failed load, so "Delete everything I kept" and "Forget tonight's paragraph" disappear on any error.

## Description
load() sets cards to null on a non-OK answer or a thrown fetch (EssayShelf.tsx:22-23), and `if (!cards) return null` (:38) draws nothing: first load, a 409 (nobody seated), a 500 and a dropped connection all render identically to "not yet loaded". The two privacy controls live inside the same block. Registry software-engineering/async-ui-states, technique failure-states: a failed request must not render as absence. Fixed looks like: a failed load keeps the controls that do not need the list (Forget tonight's paragraph) and says the shelf could not be loaded, with a retry.

## Flow
- the phone opens the Essay tab while the desk answers 500 (or the Wi-Fi drops)
- load() -> setCards(null) -> the shelf renders null
- the learner who came to delete their texts sees no shelf and no delete control, and no line saying why

## Expected impact
The learner can still forget tonight's paragraph and knows the shelf failed. Could break: a flash of the failure line on a slow first load if loading and failed are not separated.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a failed load is distinguishable and keeps its controls
Before: states that render identically (nothing): loading, 409, 500, network = 4
After: loading 1, failed 1 with the controls (predicted)
Method: simulation - three walked cases from the code; the client component has no DOM test harness in this repo
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: desk/src/app/phone/EssayShelf.tsx:22 `if (r.ok) {...} else setCards(null);` :23 `catch { setCards(null); }` :38 `if (!cards) return null;`
instrument: Extract the shelf's render decision into a pure function of {cards, failed} and pin with a rules case that a failed GET /api/texts renders a "could not load" line plus the Forget and Delete-everything controls; then the same through essay-file-live on both arms.

title: A failed exclude on /drop is silent and the route has no guard on the write
body:
## Summary
desk/src/app/drop/page.tsx:64 ignores the answer to POST /api/twin, and desk/src/app/api/twin/route.ts:54-56 lets a write failure escape as an unhandled 500.

## Description
toggle() awaits the fetch, never reads r.ok, and refreshes; a 404, 403 or 500 just snaps the checkbox back with no word, so a learner who unticked a piece may export it believing it is left out. The route calls twinState and saveTwinState with no try, so a disk error becomes Next's HTML 500 instead of a sentence. The drop page is outside this context's paths (out-of-scope), so this is a Lane B worker's.

## Flow
- on /drop, untick an exemplar while twin.json cannot be written
- POST /api/twin throws in saveTwinState -> unhandled 500
- toggle() ignores it, refreshes, the box is ticked again, nothing is said; the card still carries the text

## Expected impact
The learner knows a review choice did not stick. Could break: nothing on the happy path.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a failed review change is said
Before: failure answers shown to the learner: 0 of 3 (404, 403, 500)
After: 3 of 3 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked from the code; the route half is gate-able, the page half is out of scope
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/app/drop/page.tsx:64 `await fetch("/api/twin", {...}); setTick((t) => t + 1);`
desk/src/app/api/twin/route.ts:54-56 twinState / saveTwinState with no try
instrument: A twin-rules-test case with writeTwinFile stubbed to throw: POST /api/twin {exclude} answers a JSON 500 with a sentence and the state is unchanged; a source pin (or render) that /drop shows that sentence and leaves the box as the server holds it.

title: A Workroom build still reads every piece file four times per /api/twin GET
body:
## Summary
GET /api/twin (phone/PC) calls workroomOf (listPieces + getPiece per piece) and then listPieces + getPiece again, plus excludedOf twice.

## Description
desk/src/app/api/twin/route.ts:34-36 and desk/src/lib/twin/workroom.ts:35-37 each list and then re-read every piece, and listPieces itself parses each file (desk/src/lib/session/texts.ts:99-105). At the caps that is 4 x 50 parses of up to 2 x 100 KB JSON per GET; the residual 351 ms after the diff memo is mostly this. A cold first call after a restart still costs ~2.8 s (all diffs once). Fixed: one read per piece per request (workroomOf takes or returns the pieces it read).

## Flow
- open /drop with 50 kept pieces near the cap
- GET /api/twin -> 4 reads per piece, 2 twin.json reads
- every toggle POST rebuilds the Workroom again

## Expected impact
The desk stays responsive while an adult works their shelf. Could break: the two shelves (session and route) seeing different snapshots if not taken from one read.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - one read per piece per request
Before: reads per piece per GET: 4; steady GET at the caps ~351 ms + route reads
After: reads per piece: 1 (predicted ~4x fewer parses)
Method: simulation - read sites counted from the code; the probe exists but the route half was not timed
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/app/api/twin/route.ts:34-36 excludedOf + workroomOf + listPieces().map(getPiece)
desk/src/lib/twin/workroom.ts:35-36 listPieces + getPiece; :37 excludedOf
instrument: The wr.cjs probe (50 pieces x 2 versions x 100 KB, scratch DESK_DATA_DIR) timing GET /api/twin with a readFileSync counter, on both arms: workroomOf taking the pieces it already read, and the route reusing workroomOf's pieces.

title: The Essay TV announces neither its focus nor its caption to a screen reader
body:
## Summary
Essay Master's TV screens mark focus only with data-focused (10 sites, 0 aria-current) and the caption slot has no live region, so VoiceView reads neither the focused stop nor the caption that changes.

## Description
desk/src/essay/EssayTV.tsx and desk/src/essay/Workroom.tsx carry data-focused on every stop and render the caption in .em-cap with no aria-live. The same holds for every TV surface (desk/src/tv/screens.tsx 16 data-focused / 0 aria-current, desk/src/maths/MathsTV.tsx 14 / 0), so the fix is a TV-wide pattern (how On Air announces a focus move and a caption), not an Essay patch: Lane C as a cross-cutting choice, with the device check (a VoiceView pass on the stick) the operator's.

## Flow
- turn on VoiceView on the Fire TV stick; open Essay Master
- Up/Down move the focus; nothing is announced
- a caption changes (Reading -> verdict); nothing is announced

## Expected impact
A blind or low-vision learner can use the TV with VoiceView. Could break: chatty announcements if every caption re-render is live.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - focus and caption are announced
Before: focus sites exposed to assistive tech: 0 of 10 (Essay); live caption regions: 0
After: unmeasurable here: needs the VoiceView pass on the device
Method: probe - the site counts by grep; the outcome needs the operator's device
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence: grep data-focused: desk/src/essay/EssayTV.tsx 8, desk/src/essay/Workroom.tsx 2; aria-current|aria-selected: 0 in both; tv/screens.tsx 16/0; maths/MathsTV.tsx 14/0

title: The Essay design doc says the Workroom titles are set in a serif Specimen does not load
